## Before class

- **No new Stanton reading this week** — use the breathing room to catch up if you're behind
- **Bring a candidate dataset for your final project** (two, if you're torn) — requirements are on the [final project page](../final-project.qmd). Have the actual file(s) *downloaded to your laptop* before class; hunting for data during the workshop wastes your workshop
- Skim back over R4DS [Ch. 1–8](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/) wherever you feel shaky — today assembles all of it
- Bring your laptop

## In class

- Why real analysis is 80% preparation — and why every dataset so far arrived suspiciously clean
- The pipeline map: import → tidy → transform → visualize → model/test, tied back to the session that taught each step
- One worked pass, start to finish, on the Alaska crash data: import with type fixes, derived time-of-day variables, group summaries, two polished plots, and the Homework 5 question settled with a t-test run **both ways** — `t.test()` and `ttestBF()`
- **Most of the session is Lab 7**: the same pipeline, run on the dataset *you're* proposing for the final project — import it, audit its missingness, summarize it, plot it, and write an honest feasibility memo
- Exit ticket: your dataset's name and source, plus the biggest cleaning obstacle you hit
